LESSON: WRITING 14.5.1 DESCRIPTIVE WRITING (280 – 320 WORDS)

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.5: Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing (280 – 320 words)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing (280 – 320 words), part of Strand 14 in Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What makes a story creative? 2. Which words do we use to describe our different senses?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. use the correct writing process to write a composition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing (280 – 320 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. spell words correctly in composition writing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing (280 – 320 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. apply the five senses in writing descriptive compositions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing (280 – 320 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. display creativity and imagination in composition writing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing (280 – 320 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. recognise the importance of creativity in writing.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing (280 – 320 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. use the correct writing process to write a composition,

   Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing (280 – 320 words) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. spell words correctly in composition writing,

   Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing (280 – 320 words) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. apply the five senses in writing descriptive compositions,

   Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing (280 – 320 words) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. display creativity and imagination in composition writing,

   Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing (280 – 320 words) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. recognise the importance of creativity in writing.

   Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing (280 – 320 words) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. write sentences that describe things in the classroom using the five senses,

2. write a composition on a topic related to the World Cup,

3. in small groups, engage in relay writing and share the final product with the rest of the class,

4. read a short excerpt of writing on the World Cup from a selected writer or a writer they admire and try to write a composition, in their own words, but using the style or words learnt from the writer,

5. look at a set of pictures or items on the World Cup provided by the teacher and write a descriptive composition based on these items, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. write sentences that describe things in the classroom using the five senses,
2. write a composition on a topic related to the World Cup,
3. in small groups, engage in relay writing and share the final product with the rest of the class,
4. read a short excerpt of writing on the World Cup from a selected writer or a writer they admire and try to write a composition, in their own words, but using the style or words learnt from the writer,
5. look at a set of pictures or items on the World Cup provided by the teacher and write a descriptive composition based on these items, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing (280 – 320 words) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: It is enhanced as the learner writes creative compositions.

• Digital literacy: It is enhanced as the learner shares their compositions on the school website.

• Communication and collaboration: It is achieved as the learner engages in relay writing.

Values:
• Unity: It is promoted as the learner works with others to write group compositions.

• Responsibility: It is enhanced as the learner ensures that their part in the relay composition is well written.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Creative thinking skill: It is promoted as the learner composes descriptive compositions.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Kiswahili emphasises good composition writing skills.
